name: BlueHammer (CVE-2026-33825) â€” Windows Defender LPE Zero-Day
description: BlueHammer is a Windows local privilege escalation exploit, publicly released on April 3, 2026 by a researcher operating as 'Chaotic Eclipse' (GitHub: Nightmare-Eclipse), targeting CVE-2026-33825 â€” a time-of-check-to-time-of-use (TOCTOU) race condition in Windows Defender's threat remediation engine. The exploit plants a file that triggers Defender detection, then uses an opportunistic lock to pause Defender mid-remediation and substitutes an NTFS junction point that redirects Defender's privileged file operation into C:\Windows\System32, yielding SYSTEM-level access on fully patched Windows 10/11 hosts. Active exploitation with hands-on-keyboard activity began around April 10, 2026, prompting CISA to add CVE-2026-33825 to its Known Exploited Vulnerabilities catalog and order federal agencies to patch by May 7, 2026. BlueHammer is the first of a 'six zero-days in six weeks' disclosure spree against Microsoft Defender, alongside RedSun and UnDefend, all weaponizing Defender's own remediation logic against itself.
